name: Hopfgarten im Brixental
kurzbeschreibung: Charming market town in the Brixental valley, featuring a baroque church and lift access to the Wilder Kaiser ski area.
beschreibung:
Overview

Hopfgarten im Brixental is situated at an elevation of 622 metres in the Tyrolean lowlands within the district of Kitzbühel, scenically positioned at the entrance of the Brixental where the Kelchsauer Ache flows into the Brixentaler Ache. Encompassing roughly 166 square kilometres, it is the largest municipality by area in the district and home to around 5,800 inhabitants. The traditional market town sits nestled in a broad, sunny valley basin directly beneath the majestic peak of the Hohe Salve (1,829 m). Hopfgarten charms visitors with its heritage-listed town centre featuring cobbled alleyways and handsome historic townhouses. With direct access to the world-famous SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser – Brixental and the pristine side valley of Kelchsau, the town offers year-round recreation blending alpine adventure and rural tradition.

History

The name Hopfgarten historic originates from the early cultivation of hops in the valley. The church was first recorded on April 23, 1355, initially as a filial chapel of the ancient mother parish of Brixen im Thale. For centuries, the Brixen Valley belonged to the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg, formally integrating into the County of Tyrol only in 1816 after the Napoleonic Wars. The townscape is dominated by the monumental Baroque Parish Church of Saints James and Leonard, widely hailed as the Cathedral of the Brixen Valley (Dom des Brixentals) thanks to its striking twin-tower facade rising 52 metres. This masterpiece was constructed between 1758 and 1764 under master builders Kassian Singer and Andrä Hueber. Crowning the peak of the Hohe Salve is the Salvenkirchlein chapel, first documented in 1589 and celebrated as Austria's highest pilgrimage shrine.

Getting There

Hopfgarten boasts exemplary transport connections. By automobile, drivers take the Inntal Motorway A12 to the Wörgl-Ost exit, continuing along the federal highway B170 for just eight kilometres straight into the village centre. Railway travellers enjoy prime access via the Salzburg-Tyrol Railway: From the international rail junction at Wörgl Central Station, Tyrol S-Bahn line S8 and regional trains run frequently. With two local railway stops—Hopfgarten station and Hopfgarten Berglift, situated directly beside the cable car valley station—car-free arrival is completely effortless.

Tips

A must-do experience is riding the modern Salvenbahn gondola up to the Hohe Salve, celebrated as Tyrol's finest panoramic viewpoint offering 360-degree vistas across more than seventy 3,000-metre alpine peaks. At the summit, Austria's highest revolving restaurant, the historic Salvenkirchlein, and scenic trail loops beckon. In winter, Hopfgarten serves as an ideal springboard into the vast SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser – Brixental, featuring over 270 kilometres of groomed ski runs. In summer, families flock to the Salvenaland leisure park with its swimming lake, alpine coaster, and mini-golf. Nature lovers shouldn't miss exploring the tranquil Kelchsau side valley with its authentic wooden farms.
